To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cell wall of Mycobacteriurn tuberculosis BCG and an attenuated human isolate of M. tuberculosis is composed of 40% polysaccharides, 20% lipids, 10% proteins, 10% poly-L-glutamate, 10% L-amino acids, 5% mycolic acids, and 5% other constituents.
the chemical composition of the cell walls of five BCG strains and of one attenuated human strain is the same, and their poly-L-glutaninic acid content varies from zero to 4.5%.
The poly-L-glutamate content of the cell walls of five BCG strains and of an attenuatated human strain of M. tuberculosis is variable, ranging from 0 to about 5% of the dry weight of the cell walls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the chemical composition of cell walls of mycobacteria and the relationship between their chemical composition and their virulence.
the study of the cell walls of mycobacteria, with particular reference to the poly-L-glutaric acid present in the cell walls of the tubercle bacilli.
the chemical characterization of the cell walls of five BCG strains and of an attenuate human strain of My. tuberculosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the poly-L-glitamic acid content of the cell walls of the various strains of M. tuberculosis BCG does not seem to be a reliable indicator of their immunogenic properties.
the poly-L-glatamic acid content of the cell wall is not the sole factor determining the immunizing properties of the BCC strains.
the poly-L-glutinamic acid content of the cell wall is not related to the virulence or attenuation of the strains studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the poly-L-glutaric acid content of the cell wall is not a good indicator of the virulence of the strains.
, although the cell walls of the BCG and of the attenuated human strain are very similar, their biological properties differ.
the chemical composition of cell walls of Mycobacterius tuberculosis is not related to their pathogenicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell wall is an important factor to be considered when studying the biological properties of BCG strains.
the chemical composition of cell walls is not a suitable criterion to discriminate between the different strains of BCG.
